ic_name: DALI (Digital Addressable Lighting Interface, IEC 62386 via TI SLAA422A)
test_debug_features: QUERY STATUS (0x90) — 8 status bits returned via backward frame: bit 0 = status of control gear, bit 1 = lamp failure, bit 2 = lamp on, bit 3 = limit error, bit 4 = fade running, bit 5 = reset state, bit 6 = missing short address, bit 7 = power failure.
QUERY BALLAST (0x91) — backward 0xFF if the gear is present (used as a ping).
QUERY LAMP FAILURE (0x92) — backward 0xFF if a lamp failure is currently latched.
QUERY LAMP POWER ON (0x93) — backward 0xFF if Actual Level > 0.
QUERY LIMIT ERROR (0x94) — backward 0xFF if the last requested arc-power level was outside the [Minimum Level, Maximum Level] window.
QUERY RESET STATE (0x95) — backward 0xFF if the gear has pending reset state.
QUERY MISSING SHORT ADDRESS (0x96) — backward 0xFF if no short address is currently assigned.
QUERY VERSION NUMBER (0x97) — backward = implemented protocol version (e.g. 0x01 for IEC 62386 baseline).
QUERY CONTENT DTR (0x98) — backward = current DTR.
QUERY DEVICE TYPE (0x99) — backward = device-type code (0=fluorescent, 6=LED, 8=colour, ...).
QUERY ACTUAL LEVEL (0xA0) — backward = current Actual Level.
QUERY MAX LEVEL (0xA1) / MIN LEVEL (0xA2) / POWER ON LEVEL (0xA3) / SYSTEM FAILURE LEVEL (0xA4) — backward = stored value.
QUERY FADE TIME/RATE (0xA5) — backward = packed (FadeTime<<4) | FadeRate.
READ MEMORY LOCATION (0xC5) — backward = memory bank byte at offset (DTR1 << 8) | DTR; DTR auto-increments.
Special commands COMPARE (0xA9), VERIFY SHORT ADDRESS (0xB9), QUERY SHORT ADDRESS (0xBB) — addressing-iteration observability.

interrupt_sources.trigger: Edge detected on the DALI line — start of forward frame or mid-bit Manchester transition.
≈ 1 ms tick (SMCLK/8192) — drives fade timing and special-command timeouts.
PWM compare match enabled by TI_DALI_Update_Callback (TACCTL1 |= CCIE); ISR refreshes TACCR1/TACCR2 from LED[actual_level] and disables itself again.

interrupt_request: DALI itself does not define a global interrupt-request mechanism. In SLAA422A: Port-2 ISR captures the DALI_RX edge for Manchester decode, WDT+ interval ISR (#pragma vector=WDT_VECTOR) generates the ≈ 1 ms fade tick, and Timer_A1 ISR (#pragma vector=TIMERA1_VECTOR) handles the on-demand PWM update. Other vectors are tied to DUMMY_VECTORS via a vector-table generator in dali_demo_hw.h.
notes: DALI's observability is entirely protocol-level: every diagnostic surface (lamp failure, limit error, reset state, missing short address, fade status, power failure, version, device type, actual / min / max / power-on / system-failure / fade levels, memory-bank content) is accessible via the QUERY command family and the backward frame. There is no DFT/JTAG/scan at the protocol layer; the implementing microcontroller (MSP430F2131 / MSP430G2xx2 in the TI report) ships its own JTAG/Spy-Bi-Wire debug interface.
